title: Custom Functions in Sheets
text: These questions check that you can write and test custom functions, and explain when Sheets recalculates them and what they can't do.

tasks.text: A cell contains =KGFOR("B3", Harvests!A2:E). What does the function's second parameter receive?
choices: An array of arrays with the values in that range

tasks.text: Which can a custom function do?
choices: Return an array of arrays that spills into neighboring cells

tasks.text: =TOTALKG() reads the Harvests sheet inside its code. After new harvests are logged, the cell still shows last week's total. Explain why, and how to fix it.
tasks.answer: Sheets recalculates only when the formula's inputs change, and the formula has none it can see; the dependency is hidden inside the code. Pass the data as a range argument, e.g. =TOTALKG(Harvests!A2:E), so Sheets recalculates when that range changes.

tasks.text: Why is Shifts!A2:D better than Shifts!A2:D1000 for a range that keeps growing?
tasks.answer: A2:D is open-ended: it goes to the bottom of the sheet, so new rows are always included. A2:D1000 stops at row 1000, so rows after that would be left out.

tasks.text:
Write a custom function KGFOR(bedId, harvestsData) that returns the total kilograms for a bed, where harvestsData is the Harvests sheet's data without the header (B is Bed ID, D is Kilograms), rounded to one decimal place as a number with Math.round. Then write testKgFor, which calls it with this data and logs the result for "B2" (expected 3.7):
[["2027-04-18", "B2", "Radish", 1.2, "x"], ["2027-05-13", "B4", "Spinach", 2.4, "x"], ["2027-05-21", "B2", "Lettuce", 2.5, "x"]]

Start a new chat with your updated learner profile and the garden context. Ask for a custom function =CROPSIN(bedId, plantingsRange) that returns the crops planted in a bed, joined with commas. (1) Paste the reply. (2) Does it take the data as an argument, or read the sheet itself? Why does that matter? (3) Test it from a test function with data from the Plantings sheet, and report the result for B1 (Tomato, Basil).
tasks.answer: Full credit: identifies whether data is passed in and explains recalculation; test result reported (B1: Tomato, Basil). Replies vary; the reply may use join(), which the student should notice is new. Grade the reasoning.
